title: Harborlane - Private VPC & region constraints discovery
summary: Initial discovery focused on private deployment options: strict region residency, multi-account VPC peering vs private endpoints, transit gateway egress requirements, and KMS key management. Customer is evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private and leans toward Private for regulatory reasons; wants latency SLOs and auditability. Next steps include sharing network diagram checklist, security pack, and scheduling a 2-hour technical deep dive lab with sample model benchmark.
topics: VPC peering vs PrivateLink/private endpoint tradeoffs
transit gateway and egress IP control
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-29 16:00 PT, Duration ~52 minutes. Attendees: Miles Carter (Redwood AE), Anika Patel (Redwood SE), Tess Huang (Redwood CSM), Jorge Ramirez (CTO - Harborlane), Priya Shah (Cloud Architect), Liam O'Neill (Security), Sara Kim (Product).

00:00 - Miles: okay great everybody can hear me? Hi I'm Miles from Redwood, thanks for taking the time. we'll do a quick intros then get into your infra constraints and what success looks like.
00:12 - Jorge: Yeah, can hear you. I'll kick off — Jorge here. We're the analytics infra team at Harborlane, we run a mix of internal SaaS and customer-hosted workloads. we've been looking at inference platforms, definitely worried about data residency and egress.
00:27 - Miles: perfect. quick around the room?
00:30 - Priya: Priya, cloud architect. I own networking and VPC designs for our platform.
00:34 - Liam: Liam, security, primarily interested in key management and audit trails.
00:38 - Anika: Anika, solutions engineer — I'll be your technical lead for deeper follow ups and the bench testing.
00:44 - Sara: Sara, product, i'm leading the scoping for the assistant integration.

01:05 - Miles: Cool. To set context — Harborlane, are you evaluating hosted first and then private or are you leaning straight to private?
01:12 - Jorge: We're leaning private. We have EU residency rules and a couple of enterprise customers that insist on V P C peering or direct connect. So hosted API is attractive for speed, but legal wants the data never to leave EU-owned infra.
01:26 - Miles: understood — so region residency is a hard requirement. Do you have a preferred cloud region or account structure?
01:34 - Priya: Primary is eu-west-1 and we need to make sure all inference calls and logs stay in eu-west-1; some customers require their data in different EU countries, so we might spin multiple dedicated deployments. Also we have a multi-account landing zone — Redwood will need to either peer to a specific account or accept PrivateLink endpoints in our infra.
01:54 - Anika: Quick clarification — are you open to transit-gateway based connectivity (hub-and-spoke) or do you prefer point-to-point VPC peering?
02:02 - Priya: We'd prefer transit-gateway for scale, but some of our customers route via partner networks that only support route-table peering. so we need both options available.

02:18 - Miles: Noted. On the Private deployment, we support two main patterns: private endpoints (PrivateLink-style) deployed into your account with customer-managed DNS and private IPs, or V P C peering/reserved account model where we peer into a dedicated peered V P C. Both can be configured per-region. The tradeoffs are egress control and NATing — PrivateLink keeps endpoints but egress still can be controlled from our side, peering can allow full route control but needs more route table management.
02:48 - Liam: How do you handle egress IPs? We need stable egress IPs for allowlisting third-party services and some customers block ephemeral egress.
02:56 - Anika: We can provide static egress NAT through customer-managed egress VPC, or we can route via a transit gateway in your account so the egress IPs are stable and owned by Harborlane. There's also a dedicated egress appliance option for Dedicated deployments.
03:12 - Jorge: Good. And what about private endpoints across multiple regions? We don't want token data replicating inadvertently across regions.
03:20 - Miles: We can pin model versions and stick to region-local storage for KV cache and logs. For strict residency, the Private control plane can be customer-hosted in your VPC so metadata doesn't leave the region. We'll need to validate the logging sinks — CloudWatch vs local ELK — you prefer?
03:36 - Priya: We use Splunk on-prem and forwarders, so we'd need to send audit logs to our Splunk collectors. Also our compliance team needs proof of no cross-region replication and key usage logs.
03:48 - Liam: KMS: do you support BYOK with customer-managed keys? We want HSM-backed keys for model prompt encryption at rest.
03:55 - Anika: Yes, our Private deployment supports customer KMS/HSM integrations and we can configure envelope encryption. We emit key usage logs; we'll need to map them to your CloudTrail and KMS audit trails.
04:08 - Sara: What's the latency SLO if you run in our eu-west-1? We're planning a real-time assistant with 200-300 ms p95 target for short prompts.
04:18 - Miles: For small models and local deployment in eu-west-1 we can target sub-100 ms token latency p50 and ~200-300 ms p95 depending on batching. We'll run a bench with your realistic prompt set. Anika: we'll capture sequence length distribution and tune batching/kv cache.
04:33 - Anika: yep, we'll run token-level profiling. Important note: continuous batching improves throughput but can add tail latency; we'll tune per route for your assistant route.

05:00 - Priya: On network specifics — we need an ingress flow: app -> Harborlane VPC -> Redwood endpoint -> model. For private endpoints we need DNS entries and certs. Do you support customer-provided certs for TLS termination?
05:14 - Anika: Yes, certs can be customer-managed; private endpoints handshake will be via mTLS if you require it. We can also terminate in your VPC and send traffic over the private link.
05:25 - Miles: Quick doc reference: we'll send the network checklist that lists required security groups, route table entries, prefix lists, and port ranges.

06:00 - Jorge: On tenancy — do you run multi-tenant within a peered V P C or each customer gets isolated V P C / account? We need to prove isolation for certain regulated customers.
06:10 - Miles: For Dedicated and Private we can do single-tenant VMs per customer in a shared account or customer-account isolation. For the highest assurance customers, we recommend per-customer V P C in the customer's account with PrivateLink into their network so they're fully in control.
06:25 - Liam: And for audits — SOC2: do you provide access to audit logs and runbooks? Our auditors will need to see logs around model loads and key access.
06:33 - Anika: We have a compliance pack; it includes SOC2 artifacts, architecture diagrams, and runbooks. For Private deployments we can export the audit logs to your Splunk/ELK. We'll redact sensitive internal telemetry as needed.

06:55 - Priya: A couple of tricky bits: we use AWS Global Accelerator for low-latency peering across countries and we use centralized NAT gateways in a shared services account. Will that pattern complicate setup?
07:07 - Miles: It's common; we can peer into the shared services account or terminate endpoints there. The main thing is route propagation and ensuring your shared NAT egress IPs are reachable. We'll include a diagram showing options.
07:20 - Jorge: Competitive question: Are you aware of vendors who offer appliance-based inference tunnelling? We had a proof with another vendor that used a VPN appliance but performance sagged.
07:29 - Miles: Yes, we've seen appliance/VPN approaches — they can work but latency and maintainability suffer. We compare to Anthropic/OpenAI hosted flows for speed and to self-hosted vendors for control. We'll include competitor notes in the follow up.

08:00 - Sara: For the pilot, what would make it successful from Redwood's perspective and our perspective?
08:06 - Miles: From your side, success is meeting residency + meeting latency SLO + clear auditability. From Redwood side, success is validating we can meet p95 latency under your traffic profile and integrate logs/KMS. We'll propose a two-week pilot: deploy Private endpoints in a single eu-west-1 account, run a throughput test and a simulated workload of ~100 rps with your prompt set.
08:30 - Priya: Two asks: 1) we need a network checklist and a BGP/ASN diagram for transit-gateway; 2) we need KMS integration steps and expected key policies. Also can you share an estimate of cost for Dedicated vs Private in eu-west-1?
08:46 - Miles: We'll send a cost ballpark and a formal quote after the pilot scoping. Anika will own the technical deep dive and bench. Tess will send security docs.

09:05 - Liam: A note about egress allowlisting: some of our customers require that the inference VPC have static outbound IPs so they can whitelist; otherwise they refuse to connect. Can you promise static egress per region?
09:18 - Anika: We can provide static egress via NAT in the customer's account or via a managed egress IP pool. We'll document both patterns and their tradeoffs.
09:28 - Jorge: Good. Also we use whitelabeling of endpoints for customers, so we'll need custom DNS names mapping to private endpoints.
09:35 - Miles: That's supported via customer DNS or Route53 private hosted zones. We'll include DNS setup steps.

10:00 - [Minor crosstalk, background noise]
10:15 - Priya: one more question — do you support on-prem deployment (air-gapped) if we have a few customers in government sectors?
10:24 - Miles: We offer an on-prem package for Private; footprint and HW requirements vary by model size. For strict air-gap we'd need to schedule a separate engagement; it's doable but longer lead time.

10:40 - Sara: Regarding model versioning — do you support pinning model versions and rollbacks without redeploying infra?
10:47 - Anika: Yes, rollout control is part of the platform. You can pin to a model SHA and perform canary rollouts. We'll demo that in the deep-dive workshop.

11:05 - Jorge: Let's talk timelines — we have an internal procurement window in Q2 and want a pilot in early Q3. timeline constraints?
11:16 - Miles: That's realistic. Pilot in Q3 is doable: we'll need network prep and security review finished at least 2 weeks before pilot start. We'll aim to schedule the tech deep dive in the next 10 days.

11:40 - Priya: small nit: our infra team requires an IP allowlist for control plane or API access. Does Redwood require opening ports?
11:48 - Anika: For the Private control plane we can operate a customer-hosted control plane in your account which avoids public control plane egress. Otherwise we have a control plane API that talks via HTTPS from your VPC; we'll provide the specific FQDNs and allowlist IP ranges.
11:59 - Liam: Any mandatory ports or protocols?
12:02 - Miles: Mainly 443/TCP for control plane, and internal port ranges for gRPC/model traffic — we'll put exact ranges in the checklist.

12:30 - Miles: Ok i'm going to recap next steps before we close. Anika, Tess — you want to add?
12:36 - Anika: i'll run the bench plan and sample prompt capture. I'll need Priya's network diagram and a test account to deploy private endpoints into.
12:44 - Tess: I'll send the compliance pack and SOC2 artifacts and set up a shared folder for logs and diagrams.
12:50 - Miles: from Harborlane?
12:52 - Priya: I'll share the VPC/subnet IDs and the shared services diagram, plus a Splunk collector endpoint for logs. Expect this by Friday.
13:03 - Jorge: we'll also get the list of enterprise customers with stricter residency so you can see the multi-region needs.

13:20 - Miles: Great. we'll follow up with an email that includes: network checklist PDF, security pack, bench plan, and a proposed pilot schedule. Any final questions?
13:30 - Sara: No further questions; thanks everyone.
13:34 - Miles: Thanks all, talk soon.
13:38 - [Meeting ends]

Notes on transcription quality: some terms transcribed as separate letters (V P C, K M S) and occasional name mis-hearings of Harborlane internal services. Some timestamps approximate.
next_steps: Redwood to send network checklist and BGP/Transit diagram
Redwood to share SOC2 compliance pack and runbooks (Tess)
Schedule 2-hour technical deep-dive/bench with Anika within 10 days
Harborlane to provide VPC/subnet IDs, Splunk collector endpoint, and network diagram by Friday
Redwood to provide cost ballpark for Dedicated vs Private in eu-west-1
action_items: Anika Patel: prepare bench plan and sample prompt capture; request test account (due: 2026-04-08)
Tess Huang: send compliance pack and SOC2 artifacts; create shared secure folder (due: 2026-04-02)
Priya Shah: provide VPC/subnet IDs, shared services diagram, Splunk endpoint (due: 2026-04-03)
Miles Carter: follow up with pilot schedule and ballpark cost (due: 2026-04-06)
notes: Pilot target: two-week Private pilot in eu-west-1; success criteria: residency verified, p95 latency within 200-300ms for assistant route, logs exported to Harborlane Splunk, KMS BYOK validated. Potential blockers: multi-region customer requirements and air-gapped on-prem timelines.
